title: Lumière tout autour de nous
oneGoal: Les élèves pourront identifier différentes sources de lumière autour d'eux et comprendre qu'on a besoin de lumière pour voir.
progression: Leçon de base: Introduction à l'observation sécuritaire des sources lumineuses et leur nécessité pour la vision

opening.activity: Light detective game (5 min): Turn off all classroom lights. Ask 'Qu'est-ce qui se passe? Pourquoi ne pouvons-nous pas bien voir?' Turn lights back on. Introduce: 'Nous avons besoin de lumière pour voir!'
decisionPoints: SAFETY CRITICAL: If élèves want to look directly at bright lights or touch hot objects, immediately redirect and explain safety rules - never look at sun/bright lights, never touch hot surfaces

LIGHT SOURCES vs REFLECTION: If élèves confuse things that MAKE light (sun, lamp) with things that SHOW light (mirror, white paper), help them distinguish sources vs reflectors - critical concept for Grade 1
OBSERVATION vs INFERENCE: If élèves describe what they actually SEE (bright, dim, colorful) vs what they THINK (happy, scary, magical), encourage precise observational language about light properties
movementBreaks: Act like different sources of light - shine bright like the sun, flicker like candles, beam like flashlights (45 seconds)
Show how we move toward warmth and light - stretch toward sunshine, huddle for warmth in shadows (30 seconds)

main.activity: Light source hunt (25 min): Students explore classroom and nearby areas to find light sources. Use clipboards to draw or check off: sun through windows, overhead lights, computer screens, flashlights. Create class chart categorizing light sources. Practice vocabulary: 'Cette lumière vient du...' Students test vision by looking at books in bright vs dim areas. Compare what happens when they cover/uncover light sources.

decisionPoints: Decision Point 1: If élèves are making detailed scientific observations and recording findings accurately, challenge them to make predictions about cause and effect; if struggling with observations, guide focus to one key observable feature at a time

Decision Point 2: If élèves demonstrate safe handling of materials and follow scientific procedures De manière autonome, introduce more complex investigations; if unsafe or confused about procedures, pause for safety review et guiderd practice

Decision Point 3: If élèves are connecting observations to scientific concepts and using vocabulary correctly, extend to real-world applications; if struggling with connections, provide more scaffolded examples and vocabulary support

closing.activity: Light celebration circle (10 min): Students share their favorite light source and explain why we need it. Sing simple song about light helping us see: 'La lumière, la lumière, nous aide à tout voir!'
decisionPoints: LIGHT & VISION CONNECTION: If élèves understand that we need light to see things (not that we just see automatically), they grasp a fundamental physics concept - light must travel from source to object to eye

HEAT SAFETY UNDERSTANDING: If élèves peut identifier which objects might be hot and should not be touched (lamp bulbs, stove, sunny metal), they understand heat safety - remove this decision if lesson doesn't involve heat
Si élèves distinguent sources lumière naturelle/artificielle lors observations (soleil vs lampe), encourager classification avec preuves spécifiques observées
